text: Nine minutes until the gate closes. Two ropes drop past Sora from the high doorway into the water.
Six fresh Black Hound hunters slide down and splash in, weapons drawn.
Mok wades over to his men and turns. He wants the core, and the phone that recorded his bribe.
Jaeha, still on his knees, reminds him whose hands were on his shoulders a moment ago.
Whatever cracked in Mok has sealed over. He regrets only that Jaeha survived the first door.
He sends his men at the exhausted summons. The order: kill Jaeha, leave no witnesses.
Up in the doorway, Sora rests her chin on her crossbow like someone at the cinema.
Then a red window. He has pushed too far today, and the system cuts him back to a single link.
The light in Lyra's and Borro's eyes flickers like dying bulbs. Lyra wants to know why.
Jaeha chooses. Borro is a shield and Lyra a bow, but only Nib has ever stood alone against a horde.
Eyes still on Mok, he apologises to the other two: guard Yerin, and survive.
The glow goes out of them. Lyra drops to one knee, Borro sags on his shield, too weak to fight.
Nib, his one link left, takes five fresh minutes and steps out alone against seven. He asks the question from the night they met.
Jaeha's answer hasn't changed since that night. The order after it is new.
Mok laughs. To him, it's one battered doll versus a whole squad.
Nib doesn't even blink. Next to what he has already survived, seven men are a small job.
On the Ninth Wall he held for nine days, one small cloaked figure against a swarm.
Three hunters charge him at once, two swords and a spear.
Jaeha presses a hand to the water and closes his eyes. Not half this time. All of it.
Nib parries both swords and ducks the spear in a blur of sparks.
A blade slices across his arm. Nib doesn't flinch, and no blood comes.
Because the gash opens on Jaeha's arm instead. He doesn't make a sound.
Yerin sees what he's doing and is horrified. Lyra, in rest form and barely standing, covers them anyway.
Nib kicks the spearman's legs out and drives a hilt into a swordsman's jaw.
An arrow hits him in the thigh.
Jaeha's thigh bleeds right where it struck. Carry at a hundred and forty percent, and he falls onto his hands.
Nib pulls the arrow out, snaps it in one hand, and keeps walking.
Up in the doorway, Sora leans forward. Her compass blazes, pointing straight at Nib.
A violet bolt from the mage's staff blasts Nib across the water.
A burn spreads down Jaeha's forearm, and he sags toward the water. Borro's huge hand catches him.
Borro crouches over Jaeha, shell overhead, shield in front. Jaeha once promised him a roof. Now Borro is one.
Smoking, Nib gets up and walks back into the middle of the seven.
This time Mok himself slashes, and catches Nib's cheek below the mask.
Under Borro's shell, a cut opens across Jaeha's cheek. His eyes never leave Nib.
Nib touches his cheek and finds no blood. He looks back at Jaeha and understands.
Jaeha smiles through it, as if this is the deal working exactly as designed.
Five minutes forty until the gate closes.
And the amber in Nib's eye burns brighter, and brighter.
The hunters back away from the light pouring off him. Holding the line has broken another seal: three of five.
Armour assembles out of the light, wall-blue and bronze, with the nine-tower sigil on one pauldron. His knives lengthen into a scout-captain's long knives.
In one turn, Nib cuts both swordsmen's grips and belts, and their swords splash into the water.
A bronze bracer to the temple, and one folds into the water, out cold.
One leap cuts the archer's bowstring and the spear in half.
He pins the spearman under one bare foot, knife at his throat, not touching. Nib isn't here to kill anyone.
The mage fires again. Nib cuts the bolt in half in mid-air.
He slices the staff into three pieces and catches its core as it falls. The mage's hands go up.
The shield-bearer from the grain silo charges. Nib vaults over him, and he runs straight into the rubble.
Six hunters, disarmed, and every single one alive. Only Mok is left standing.
Nib faces him across the water and, very politely, lets Mok go first.
Mok charges behind his cracked tower shield with a roar.
Nib meets him and drives both long knives, crossed, into the crack down its middle.
The shield splits in two, its hollow grip snaps, and Mok falls on his back in the water.
Nib stands over him, knife a finger's width from his throat. Killing him isn't Nib's call. Mok belongs to Jaeha.
The clock says four minutes ten.
Yerin and Lyra haul Jaeha out, bleeding from four wounds and grinning. Lyra is openly jealous of Nib's outfit.
Then something wrapped in plastic and tape slides out of the snapped grip into the water.
Mok's face goes white. A knife at his throat didn't scare him like this. That package does.
Jaeha pulls free and crawls to it on his knees.
His shaking hands tear it open: an old phone in a cracked orange case, a faded stick figure in a vest on the back, thumbs up.
The same stick figure Minseok doodled in the first pages of Jaeha's notebook.
Jaeha's eyes fill with tears. He would know that sticker anywhere.
Mok turns his face away. Nib asks what everyone is thinking: why keep it hidden, all this time?
Up in the doorway, Sora steps back out of the torchlight. Gone.
After four years, the cracked screen flickers to life, its battery almost empty.
It still holds one thing from Minseok's last night: a single video.
